content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (sentiment > 0.67) and especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (sentiment < 0.33) or shows strong negative momentum; adjust downward bias.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., >75.00) and then fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” factor to subsequent days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days prior, model often overreacts — dampen forecast by 3–5% for that horizon.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extrapolating from 18-day history without sentiment confirmation — if sentiment is neutral or declining, reduce forecast volatility.
